messages:
sophia-ml: Quick share — ran an activation-tail detector + dynamic-clamp sweep on star-7b using AWQ int8. Found a small set of layers with persistent heavy-tail channels that explain most of the quality delta vs FP16. initial lm_eval delta: -0.72%
raj-kumar: Which layers showed the tails? any pattern (attn vs ffn)?
sophia-ml: Mostly FFN layers (layers 5, 8, 12, 14, 17). tail channels are sparse (<0.5% channels per layer) but magnitude >> sigma. Looks like occasional activation spikes during long-context QA.
maria-g: Can you paste the detection code? want to reproduce locally.
sophia-ml: Sure — simple detector we used (runs on activations saved from a small eval set):
```python
# activation-tail detection (toy)
import numpy as np
th = 3.5  # z-score threshold
tails = {}
for l in range(L):
    act = activations[l]  # shape: [batch, seq, channels]
    ch_mean = act.mean(axis=(0,1))
    ch_std = act.std(axis=(0,1)) + 1e-6
    z = (act - ch_mean) / ch_std
    mask = np.abs(z).max(axis=(0,1)) > th
    tails[l] = np.where(mask)[0].tolist()
```
This gives per-layer channel indices to inspect. We used th=3.5 after sweeping 2.5-5.0.
alex-p: How did you mitigate in quant path — clamp or skip-channel fallback?
sophia-ml: Two modes tried: 1) per-channel dynamic clamp before quant (clamp to ch_mean +/- k*ch_std, k=3.5) 2) skip-quant on offending channels (keep fp16 weights/activations for that channel, emulates a GPTQ rescue).
maria-g: Results? numbers?
sophia-ml: Eval summary from the small suite (500 prompts):
- FP16 baseline accuracy: 85.20
- AWQ int8 baseline: 84.48  (delta -0.72)
- AWQ + dynamic-clamp (k=3.5): 85.03 (delta -0.17)
- AWQ + skip-channel for tail channels: 85.10 (delta -0.10)
Latency: clamp adds ~0.6% token-time, skip-channel adds ~1.8% due to mixed code-paths.
So clamp recovers most accuracy with much smaller perf hit.
raj-kumar: Nice. Did you try per-layer thresholds (adaptive) vs single k?
sophia-ml: Yes — adaptive k per-layer (fit to 99.9th percentile of z) reduced false positives and kept clamping tighter. That variant gave 85.08 and slightly lower perf cost than global k.
eval-bot: [AUTO] full-run logs uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-evals/star-7b/awq/activation-clamp/1815000000/logs.tar.gz
alex-p: Any firmware/runtime changes needed for clamp? or can we deploy as small pre-quant pass?
sophia-ml: Implemented as a lightweight pre-quant pass in the offline compiler — emits per-channel clamp parameters into the quant table and runtime applies clamp just before quantization op. No kernel recompile required. For skip-channel we route the offending channels through the slower fp16 kernel path (requires mixed-kernel support we already have).
maria-g: Next steps? want to add this to the bakeoff checklist.
sophia-ml: Proposed plan:
- Add activation-tail detector to onboarding harness (optional, opt-in)
- Default dynamic-clamp sweep: k in [2.5,3.5,4.5], adaptive-k per-layer option
- Measure perf/accuracy tradeoffs across 3 workloads (chat, long-context QA, summarization)
- If skip-channel improves >0.15% w.r.t clamp for a customer, enable skip fallback in rollout policy

Action items: @raj-kumar will add detector to the harness (PR draft), @alex-p will prototype runtime flag to toggle clamp table, @maria-g will add the three workloads to bakeoff matrix.
sophia-ml: TL;DR — clipping/clamp is an easy win for these rare heavy-tail channels, recovers most of the AWQ delta with tiny perf cost. Skip-channel is better quality but costlier. Will push experimental PRs this week. :rocket:
raj-kumar: SG, will start the PR today. :thumbsup:
